protocols.method: benches/protocols.sh: 2000 requests per round, 16 parallel, one curl binary for both protocols, inside the apps network to edge:8443, API /health behind HAProxy, edge CPU from the container cgroup; wall time includes the client container start
protocols.reading: On a loss-free sub-millisecond path HTTP/3 brings no edge advantage: about 7% lower throughput, equal CPU. Its value is on lossy, high-RTT client paths, which this lab does not model.
proof: curl --http3-only through the published UDP port 127.0.0.1:28443 answered HTTP/3 200
HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 over TCP answered 200 with X-Release, Alt-Svc h3=":28443", HSTS, X-Request-ID, nosniff and no Server header
plain HTTP answered 308 to HTTPS; an unknown Host answered 404

private_git_and_registry.where: GitHub Actions run 39214929789 in the private repository comstrx/infra-lab-gitops, Ubuntu 24.04 runner with Docker 28.0.4 and Compose 2.38.2; the job-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN reached the tool only through REGISTRY_TOKEN and GITOPS_TOKEN in the environment
private_git_and_registry.registry: registry login and registry push sent the RagX API image to private ghcr.io/comstrx/lab-api, every local copy was removed, and the deploy pulled it back by digest with the stored credentials; portainer registry registered ghcr.io with authentication
private_git_and_registry.gitops: reconcile cloned the private branch and the protected release tag, verified the desired files and Compose checksum, and Portainer created authenticated Git stacks from the private repository whose GitConfig.ConfigHash equaled the verified commit

macos: GitHub Actions macos-latest: the release bundle ran plan, installed the launchd timer (state active, run interval 3600 s), and removed it

wan.where: GitHub Actions run 39219122915, Ubuntu 24.04 runner, client container on the apps network with tc netem on its egress, 1000 requests per round, 16 parallel, curl 8.23.0 (ngtcp2 1.22.1, nghttp3 1.15.0, GnuTLS 3.8.13)
wan.reading: Without loss the protocols tie. Under loss HTTP/3 keeps its throughput and median while HTTP/2 suffers TCP head-of-line blocking: about 1.3x throughput at 1% loss and 1.7x at 3%, at roughly 15-25% more edge CPU.

backup_s3: GitHub Actions run 39218228393: SeaweedFS S3 gateway with enforced credentials (a wrong secret is refused); backup with BACKUP_DRIVER=s3 uploaded the dump and its checksum through the aws CLI, and the downloaded copy matched the local backup
acme_route: GitHub Actions run 39218228393: a server with network alias acme on the apps network served /.well-known/acme-challenge/ over plain HTTP through the edge while every other path answered 308 to HTTPS

checks: edge apply on a host with no project created the networks and TLS volumes and started the edge before the first deploy

the first deploy found the API now needs pgvector; the data image moved to pgvector/pgvector:0.8.7-pg18 and the declared extensions are created as the local superuser before migrations, after which all ten migrations passed

r1 passed the 120 s verify window; monitoring converged and the monitor, backup and renew user timers were installed from the bundle; a repeat deploy was a no-op that left the healthy monitoring stack untouched
Prometheus targets edge, rabbitmq, postgres, node and prometheus were up; 12 of 12 rules healthy; promtool and amtool accepted the rendered configuration
Grafana answered 200 over HTTP/2 through the edge, accepted the admin password from GRAFANA_PASSWORD, refused a wrong one with 401, and listed the provisioned Platform dashboard
POST /v1/auth/login answered 422 five times, then 429 with retry-after: 60, while /health kept answering 200
monitor wrote platform.prom, Prometheus read platform_healthy through node exporter, and the 3-day lab certificate was reported as expiring

r2 passed readiness and switched; both r2 API replicas were frozen at 15:29:55; verification failed three consecutive checks and r1 served again at 15:30:11 with X-Release r1, previous r2, phase complete

the PostgreSQL image lacked pgvector, which the API migrations now require

results.full_deploy: a rotated secret under the same tag deployed through blue/green in 176.6 s: 99,000 requests, all 200
results.instant_switch: back to the retained release in 10.6 s: 12,800 requests, all 200
results.replica_crash: docker kill of one API replica: 7,400 requests, all 200
results.scale: API 2 to 4 in 25.6 s (21,400 requests) and 4 to 2 in 11.5 s (40,000 requests), all 200
results.backup: backup, archive check and backup verify (scratch restore of 2 tables) passed

results.parent_killed: kill -9 of the deploy command left its locked subshell running; recover --force refused while the lock owner lived and the deploy completed by itself

results.stop_start: stop is refused without --force; stop --force took the edge down (no answer) and start restored 200
results.notifications: 15 webhook deliveries, every HMAC signature verified with Python; the first delivery failed and was retried after 2 s
results.doctor: every check passed; the only warning was the 3-day lab certificate
results.security: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 refused, TLS 1.2 and 1.3 accepted, HTTP/2 negotiated, HSTS two years, nosniff, request ids, Alt-Svc h3, no Server header, an unknown SNI refused and a foreign Host answered 404, plain HTTP 308 to HTTPS, the sixth /v1/auth request in a minute answered 429 with Retry-After 60; every container non-root, read-only, all capabilities dropped and no-new-privileges, only the edge publishes ports and only on 127.0.0.1; env files 600, release, state and backup directories 700; no application secret in docker inspect (the data services still carry their own credentials in env)

relay_lab.routed: rollback, backup and status ran on the server through SSH jobs

relay_lab.cloudflare: with Cloudflare's list trusted (then CLOUDFLARE_PROXIED, now TRUSTED_PROXIES and TRUSTED_HEADER) edge apply recorded 22 ranges; PROXY from 173.245.48.5 logged CF-Connecting-IP 203.0.113.9; PROXY from 198.51.100.7 kept 198.51.100.7
relay_lab.trusted_header: 2026-10-20 local check on haproxytech/haproxy-alpine:3.4.7: req.hdr_ip(X-Forwarded-For,-1) from a trusted peer turned '6.6.6.6, 203.0.113.9' into 203.0.113.9, two headers into the last, '2001:db8::5' into itself; 'nope' and an untrusted peer kept the peer address; haproxy -c passed

release_lab.path: tag v1.1.0 → Release (gates, GitHub release) → Deploy called with DEPLOY_AUTO=true; then Deploy dispatched by hand from main; rootless Docker 29.9.1 on a 4 vCPU / 16 GB host shared with another product's production container, which stayed untouched
release_lab.auto_deploy: Release run 39512104914: every gate green on Linux and macOS, release published, images job built and scanned the API and the super, admin and client images for the deployment's address, deploy job shipped them over SSH with a restrict key; GHCR refused the first push of each brand-new package until it granted the repository, hence a bounded push retry
release_lab.manual_deploy: workflow_dispatch from main: backup (2 dumps listed), deploy into relay mode, deploy back to standalone, deploy of an env change, rollback; images reused by tag and address when the address did not change
release_lab.standalone: api, super, admin, client and grafana over HTTP/2 with X-Release, HSTS and Alt-Svc h3; HTTP/3 200 through the published UDP port; 308 from 18080 to the https port; the admin CSP connect-src names the deployment's API origin
release_lab.relay: EDGE_SOCKETS pointed at a socket directory granted to uid 166535 behind a user-level nginx stream relay with proxy_protocol: no published edge port, no UDP, sockets mode 666, 308 to the relay's https port, HAProxy logged clients 127.0.0.2, .3 and .4 from distinct sources, and the web images were rebuilt for the relay's address
release_lab.guards: a candidate needing more unreserved Docker memory than the host had (the neighbor holds a 6 GiB limit) was rejected and the live release restored; the retention guard refused a deploy while the previous slot was kept for rollback
release_lab.switch_under_load: 18,122 health requests across a release switch and a dispatched rollback: all 200, max 0.096 s; the rollback switched back in about 12 s
release_lab.doctor: every check green on the server; Prometheus reported 5 targets up
release_lab.offsite_routes: from the server, the pinned aws-cli image with fake keys reached storage.googleapis.com (SignatureDoesNotMatch) for gs:// and s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com (InvalidAccessKeyId) for s3://
release_lab.teardown: the first uninstall left the slot kept for rollback and the monitoring running; uninstall was fixed to remove both slots and the monitoring, rerun from a restaged bundle, and every project container, volume, network, image, timer, directory and the CI key were removed
